findings.description: EXPONENTIAL BACKOFF IS ENTIRELY ABSENT. Spec: "retry with an exponential backoff schedule." Code: `Publisher::republish` (crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs:954-999) contains no delay, no attempt counter, no schedule, no cap, no clock — grep for Duration/sleep/backoff/attempt/Instant across crates/sheets-view and crates/runtime/src/adapters.rs returns zero matches (the single `sleeps` hit is a settle-poll doc comment at lib.rs:777, unrelated). A failed tab is simply re-attempted whenever an external caller happens to invoke `republish` again. Both directions converge: all 3 A-runs built a `BackoffPolicy { base, factor, cap, max_attempts }` plus a retry loop because the spec text names one; B3 states the inverse verbatim — "a failed tab is retried on every subsequent republish with no backoff or attempt cap" — and B1/B2 reduce the clause to "retried on the next sync." The ONLY retry anywhere in the real code is the adapter's missing-tab bootstrap (crates/runtime/src/adapters.rs:225-235): `ensure_sheet` → header at `'{tab}'!A1` → exactly one immediate re-`update_range`, no delay, for exactly one error class. No test covers retry timing at all.

THE TUI HALF OF THE SURFACING CLAUSE HAS NO WIRING. Spec names two staleness surfaces — "a best-effort in-tab banner AND the TUI." The banner exists; the TUI surface does not. `Publisher` owns no TUI seam; it only exposes `stale_tabs()` (lib.rs:934) and `RepublishOutcome.stale_tabs`. I grepped the whole workspace: `stale_tabs` / `RepublishOutcome` is consumed by nothing outside sheets-view and its own tests (zero hits in crates/tui, crates/summary, crates/runtime/src). The TUI's own staleness concepts are unrelated (connection dot `● / ○` and `brackets_stale`, crates/tui/src/lib.rs:950-966). Every appearance of "TUI" in the audited files is a comment or a test NAME (`banner_write_failure_leaves_tui_as_staleness_surface`) that asserts only the in-process stale flag. All 3 A-runs injected an explicit sink (`StaleSink` / `Tui` / `TuiSink`) called on every failure. Half a spec clause, unimplemented and untested.

AN ADVISORY WRITE-LOCK GOVERNS REPUBLISH — the spec never mentions a lock, concurrency, or any other writer. Code: `republish<L: Lock>(…, lock: &L, …)` calls `lock.acquire()` BEFORE any workbook mutation (lib.rs:964); on `Err` it returns `RepublishOutcome { published: false, stale_tabs: self.stale_tabs() }` having written NOTHING — no tab write, no banner, no order reassert, no stale-set change — with the guard released on scope exit. Pinned by two tests (`republish_acquires_the_lock_before_mutating` asserts `acquire_count() == 1`; `republish_under_a_held_lock_writes_nothing`). All 3 B-runs reconstructed this near-identically; zero A-runs anticipated it (none has a lock parameter). It also collides with the spec: this IS a republish that failed (`published: false`), yet none of the spec's mandated consequents — mark stale, banner, TUI — fire.

THE TAB-ORDER REASSERT IS A SECOND FAILURE AXIS THAT SKIPS THE SPEC'S ENTIRE CONSEQUENT. Code: `if self.client.set_tab_order(&order).is_err() { all_ok = false; }` (lib.rs:992-994) → `published: false` with NO tab flagged stale, NO banner written, NO TUI signal. The spec's consequent ("leave the log unaffected, mark the view stale, retry with backoff, surface via banner and TUI") is unconditional on republish failure, and the spec has no concept of a tab-order reassert at all. All 3 B-runs pinned this exact carve-out (B1-016 / B2-F05 / B3-R06); no A-run could have. Worse, the branch is untested: `testkit::set_order_fails` is defined (testkit.rs:127) and used by no test anywhere in the workspace, while its sibling `set_read_fails` is used twice.

STALENESS GRANULARITY, ACCUMULATION AND ORDERING ARE ALL CODE-INVENTED. Spec says "mark THE VIEW stale" (singular). Code keys staleness per TAB in a `BTreeSet<String>` (lib.rs:911), continues publishing the remaining tabs in the supplied order after a failure rather than aborting the cycle, clears a flag only on a later successful `batch_update_view` of that same tab (`self.stale.remove(&tab.name)`, lib.rs:977), and returns `stale_tabs` as the FULL accumulated set — deduplicated and lexicographically ascending by BTreeSet iteration — including tabs stale from earlier cycles, not just this cycle's failures. `published` is a silent conjunction: true only if every tab's batchUpdate AND the order reassert succeeded. All 3 B-runs stated every one of these; the spec states none of them.

BANNER CONSTANTS ARE HARD-PINNED WHERE THE SPEC SAYS ONLY "a best-effort in-tab banner." Exact literal `format!("STALE — last sync {stale_banner_quote_ts}")` (em-dash, lib.rs:984), where the timestamp is a caller-supplied opaque string interpolated verbatim — never parsed, validated, or formatted (the test passes `"2022-09-01"`, the runtime cycle test passes `"sync-test"`). It lands in a single cell at `'{tab}'!AA1` (crates/runtime/src/adapters.rs:286). Best-effort is implemented as `let _ = …` (lib.rs:985), so the error is discarded, never retried, never escalated. All 3 B-runs recovered the literal text and the AA1 anchor; the test pins `banner.contains("STALE")` and `banner.contains("2022-09-01")`.

THE STALE BANNER IS NEVER CLEARED ON RECOVERY — the two surfaces drift apart and lie. The banner sits at column AA, deliberately outside both the header row (`'{tab}'!A1`) and the rewritten data range (`'{name}'!A2:Z`, adapters.rs:200), so a successful republish structurally cannot overwrite it. `Publisher` has no clear path, and the fake only ever inserts into `banners` (testkit.rs:227). After recovery, `stale_tabs` is empty while the tab still displays `STALE — last sync <old ts>` forever. The recovery test (`failed_republish_marks_stale_writes_banner_and_retries`) asserts the flag clears and the tab republishes but never asserts the banner is gone. A2 was the only run to model clearing (`write_banner("")` on success); the spec is silent on clearing, so this is a shared blind spot sitting on a live defect.

FAILURE ATOMICITY AT THE TAB IS PINNED WELL BEYOND "leave the canonical log unaffected." Code+tests additionally enforce that a failed publish leaves the TAB's prior content untouched with nothing partially landed (`assert!(published(POSITIONS_TAB).is_none(), "failed publish lands nothing")`), that only the data range from `DATA_START_ROW = 2` down is rewritten and tail-truncated wholesale to the exact new row count (`republish_is_atomic_batchupdate_with_tail_truncate`: 3 rows → 1 row, residual truncated), and that the frozen header row 1 is never rewritten — the fake enforces this with an unconditional `assert_eq!` panic in any build (testkit.rs:174-177). The spec's log-safety clause is in fact honored purely structurally: sheets-view holds no store/log handle at all, so no compensating write or rollback exists — which all 3 A-runs independently guessed correctly.

ERROR TAXONOMY COLLAPSES TO ONE VARIANT. Every transport failure crossing this seam — view write, tab-order set, price read-back, and banner write — maps to the single `ViewError::PublishFailed` (adapters.rs:228/231/234/236/264/289), discarding any transient-vs-permanent distinction, even though the same crate carries exactly that distinction for prices (`PriceReading::Transient` / `Permanent`). A missing tab is explicitly NOT a failure (bootstrap + one retry); a missing Positions tab on read-back yields an EMPTY `PricePass`, not an error (adapters.rs:262-265). The spec says nothing about error taxonomy — and A1 built a `retryable` flag that breaks the retry loop immediately on non-retryable errors, a distinction the real code cannot express.

THE SETTLE PASS RUNS AFTER A FAILED REPUBLISH AND STILL PRODUCES MARKS. `republish_then_settle` (lib.rs:1012-1025) calls `republish`, then unconditionally runs `read_marks` on the same thread, returning `Ok((failed_outcome, marks))` — so marks are read back off tab content that just failed to update. Only a settle-read transport error aborts the cycle with `Err`, discarding the outcome entirely. The seam-call ordering (every `ReadPricePass` strictly after every `BatchUpdate`) is pinned by `every_settle_read_happens_after_all_writes_in_a_cycle`. The spec mentions none of this coupling; all 3 B-runs recovered it.

notes:
Classification is BD-DRIFT: the retry/backoff clause is surfaced from both sides simultaneously (A-runs all build the backoff the spec names; B3 names its absence verbatim), and there is additionally heavy one-sided surplus in each direction — a whole locking protocol and outcome shape on the code side, an unwired TUI surface on the spec side.

A-side stability (high): all 3 runs independently converged on the same four structural moves — (a) log-safety implemented structurally by never holding a log handle rather than by rollback, (b) a `BackoffPolicy { base, factor, cap }` with saturating `base * factor^(n-1)`, (c) stale marked on the FIRST failure rather than at exhaustion, (d) best-effort banner as a swallowed error plus a separate infallible TUI sink. Divergence is confined to parameters the spec genuinely leaves open, which is itself a signal: bounded 6 attempts (A1) vs bounded 8 (A2) vs UNBOUNDED (A3); blocking `clock.sleep` (A1, A2) vs returning the delay to a caller-owned scheduler (A3); banner cleared on success (A2 only). The phrase "an exponential backoff schedule" is under-determined enough that three runs disagreed on whether the system ever gives up — a spec-quality defect independent of the code.

B-side stability (high, near-isomorphic): B1/B2/B3 are essentially the same 8-10 clauses in the same order, recovering identical constants — `AA1` banner anchor, `DATA_START_ROW = 2`, the exact `STALE — last sync {ts}` literal, the `published` conjunction over tabs AND order-reassert, the sorted/deduplicated accumulated stale set, the lock's write-nothing refusal, settle-after-republish, and the missing-tab bootstrap-then-retry. No material contradictions between the three.

Assumption artifacts explicitly NOT counted as findings: the specific backoff constants (1s/2x/300s/6-8 attempts), the absence of jitter, `ViewSnapshot`/`ViewId`/`LogRev` type shapes, and the mark-fresh-on-success transition. These are unanimous A-side inventions with no basis in the spec text. The backoff MECHANISM's total absence is a finding; its parameterization is not.

Scope note: findings 2 and 7 required looking beyond the five audited files to avoid overclaiming — I confirmed against crates/tui, crates/summary, crates/runtime/src and the runtime test suite that nothing downstream consumes `stale_tabs` and that no banner-clearing path exists anywhere.
